key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Sudden, often at REST or during SLEEP. LOCATION: Retrosternal or left chest. RADIATES to arm, jaw, shoulder. DURATION: Brief, typically 5-15 minutes. CHARACTER: Squeezing, pressure, tightness. AGGRAVATING: Occurs at REST, often at NIGHT or EARLY MORNING (circadian pattern). NOT typically exertional. RELIEVING: Nitroglycerin (rapid response), calcium channel blockers. TIMING: Cyclic, often same time each day/night. SEVERITY: 6-8/10. KEY POSITIVES: Occurs at rest (especially 12am-8am), young to middle-aged, smoker, rapid relief with nitrates, ST elevation during episode that resolves. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT exertional angina, NOT persistent.

red_flags: Prolonged episode >20 minutes (may be myocardial infarction )
